                      Ransomware Indicators & Tripwires

                      Surfaces mass extension anomalies, ransom note stems, and decoy Canary tripwire tampering.

                      If a ransomware family was identified, check nomoreransom.org (typed by you into a browser) for a known decryptor. C.U.R.E cannot decrypt files and never links out.

                      No Ransom Activity Detected

                      User directories, Downloads, and Canary honey-decoy tripwires show zero mass encryption or note creation signatures.

                      Ransom indicators are point-in-time. To watch what actually starts after login, run a bounded live observation — it installs nothing and modifies nothing.

                            EVIDENCE-FIRST · NON-DESTRUCTIVE

                            Safely relieve C: drive pressure by identifying and guiding the migration of large personal data libraries to secondary storage (D:) with bit-exact verification.

                                              POST-LOGIN OBSERVATION · CORRELATION

                                              Login Observation

                                              Observe what actually starts after login and correlate it with recorded startup persistence. Observation installs nothing and modifies nothing.

                                              STEP 1 — PREPARE · OBSERVATION WINDOW

                                              C.U.R.E. will observe startup activity for a limited period. Observation installs nothing and modifies nothing — no Startup, registry, service, or task changes. For true post-login capture, start the observation within a minute of logging in; a reboot flow is intentionally not offered.

                                              Each choice passively records process starts/exits and window titles/classes only — no screenshots, no keystrokes, no window contents. Longer windows catch more activity but keep this screen busy.

                                              Observe for:

                                              INCIDENT STATUS

                                              —
                                              What do DIRECT / STRONG / PARTIAL / WEAK / NONE mean?
                                              • DIRECT — finding's executable path matches the observed executable path (normalized). Service entries additionally require the reported PID to match. Matched path + process.
                                              • STRONG — finding command and observed command line reference each other (executable substring either direction, or shared distinctive arguments ≥12 chars) with the launch inside the window. Matched command/path + timing.
                                              • PARTIAL — same executable file name, different paths (both shown). Matched name only.
                                              • WEAK — same folder but different program, or a child of a correlated process. Temporal/structural proximity only.
                                              • NONE — no observed relationship.

                                              Correlation does not by itself establish malicious intent. Levels and verdicts are deterministic — see the methodology note in the report export.

                                              OBSERVATION WINDOW / SCOPE

                                                Command lines are fetched only for correlated processes (bounded). Window evidence is titles + classes only — no screenshots, no keystrokes, no contents.

                                                TIMELINE — WHAT WAS OBSERVED, WHEN

                                                Each event shows its timestamp and, where the backend collected it, the process, PID, PPID, path, command line, correlation, and window. Unavailable values say “Not collected”. Long values truncate visually — hover or focus to see the full value; all evidence text is selectable.

                                                          INSUFFICIENT OBSERVATION — WHAT TO DO NEXT

                                                          Observation could not run or produced no usable data. This is not a clean bill of health.

                                                          • Re-run with a longer window (60 or 120 sec) and keep the machine otherwise idle — popups welcome.
                                                          • Start the observation within a minute of logging in for true post-login capture.
                                                          • If the failure persists, check elevation (standard-user scans may skip system locations) and re-run elevated to compare counts.
                                                          • Export the report anyway — it records the failed/unavailable observation so the gap is auditable.

                                                          LIMITATIONS — WHAT COULD NOT BE OBSERVED

                                                          • Sub-500 ms processes may be missed (snapshot + WMI delivery timing).
                                                          • Command lines are collected only for correlated PIDs.
                                                          • PIDs are re-validated before any action; PID reuse is handled, not assumed.
                                                          • No persistence or reboot capture — observation installs nothing.
                                                          • Window/process lifetimes carry ±500 ms poll precision where applicable.

                                                          EXPORT REPORT — KEEP THE EVIDENCE

                                                          JSON/TXT incident report: investigation id, elevation, coverage, timeline, window events, correlations, findings.
